result.result:
The Master's ETA of 31 Jan 2025 11:00 UTC for Sept-Iles is consistent with the 1503.8 nm to go at 12.5 kn (computed 12:18 UTC, within the 2-hour tolerance), so no charter-party ETA notice is due: the ETA moved only 5 hours, within the 12-hour change limit, and days-to-ETA 4.96 means no notice threshold in the CP is reached after the last 5-day notice (sent 25 Jan 2025 12:30 UTC with ETA 31 Jan 06:00 UTC to the agent).

The remarks explain a main-engine stop 0610–1140 UTC on 26 Jan 2025 (5.5 h) with VLSFO 1.1 t used, filters choked with sludge stirred up in heavy weather; check_stoppage agrees with the report (the speed over the remaining 18.5 steaming hours reproduces the 231.3 nm distance run), so no query to the Master is needed. Judged against the CP off-hire clause — time lost through breakdown of machinery or equipment is off hire, with off-hire bunkers for the owners' account — this stop is off hire; the cause may lie in fuel supplied by the charterer, which the owner may argue, but that claim is the operator's to make.

Simulated hire-statement figures (made up for this demo; nothing is entered): hire deducted US$ 2,177.08 (5.5 h at US$ 9,500/day) plus VLSFO 1.1 t at US$ 600/t = US$ 660, total US$ 2,837.08 to the owners' account for 2025-01-26T06:10:00Z–2025-01-26T11:40:00Z. If the operator decides to put the ship off hire and notify the owner Tormar Bulk Carriers, that would mean (a) a voyage management system off-hire entry for that period via propose_entry, and (b) an e-mail to the owner's vessel technical management giving the period and reason and asking for the engine log extract for the stop.
